events.type: background, new to the record: NVIDIA bought $2.0bn of convertible preferred stock
events.summary: Note 14 of the fiscal-2026 10-K says that on 2026-03-02 Lumentum sold about 2.9 million Series A convertible preferred shares to NVIDIA Corporation in a private placement at $695.31 each, $2.0 billion in cash. Each preferred share converts one-for-one into common stock: at NVIDIA's option once the US antitrust (Hart-Scott-Rodino) waiting period ends, or automatically on a sale to a non-affiliate. It gets the same dividends as common stock. It votes with common stock except in director elections. It has no liquidation preference, no redemption right and no preemptive right. The proxy shows 2,876,415 preferred shares outstanding on 2026-09-24, equal to about 3.2% of the 90,582,856 common shares (arithmetic). Separately, the 10-K says every series of Lumentum's convertible notes (2026, 2028, 2029, 2032) 'remain convertible at the option of the holders during the first quarter of fiscal year 2027', with principal to be settled in cash. The 2032 notes carry a $187.77 conversion price, a $1,256.1M carrying value and a $5,411.1M estimated fair value.
events.why_it_matters: This is not news in the window (it is in the 10-K of 2026-08-14), but it is missing from the thesis and the news log. Santi's thesis counts only the bond-swap dilution. Lumentum's biggest AI customer-partner owns a $2bn stake. That supports the demand story, but it is also roughly 3.2% more potential shares. The remaining convertible notes can still add shares as they convert. Neither is a new issue, so trigger 6 is not hit, but both are relevant to pillar 5.

products.name: Optical circuit switch (OCS)
products.what_it_is: A box that redirects beams of light between fibres using tiny moving mirrors. It lets a data center rewire which servers talk to which without turning the light into electricity.
products.analogy: A railway switching yard that moves the tracks instead of unloading and reloading every train.
products.buyers: Hyperscale cloud companies building AI clusters. Third-party analysis names Google as the main customer at scale; the company has not confirmed this.
products.how_it_works: Micro-mirrors steer incoming light to the chosen output fibre. Because the signal stays as light, the switch saves power and works at any data speed.
products.sales: Not separately reported. The company now says OCS is 'rapidly scaling past a $100 million quarterly revenue run rate' and expects 'revenue in the billions in upcoming years' (shareholder letter, 2026-10-06). Proxy: Systems segment revenue was $1.01bn in FY2026 (+90.7%), which includes OCS and transceiver modules.
products.size_for_company: At $100 million a quarter, OCS is about 8% of the guided $1.225-1.275bn quarterly revenue (inference from cited figures).
products.competition: Coherent and others are developing OCS; Google has built its own in the past (not verified in this run).
products.why_investors_care: It is a new, fast-growing product line that management now says could reach billions of dollars. Citi forecast an $11bn OCS market by 2030 (2026-09-28, tier 3).
products.watch_next: OCP Global Summit talk on 2026-10-14 (zero-touch OCS fabrics); whether Q1 FY2027 results on 2026-11-05 put a number on OCS revenue or name customers.

products.name: Ultra-high-power lasers / external light source (ELS) for co-packaged optics (CPO)
products.what_it_is: Very powerful continuous lasers that sit outside the switch chip and feed light to optical engines packaged right next to it.
products.analogy: One central power station feeding many houses, instead of every house running its own generator.
products.buyers: Switch and GPU system makers. Stifel says NVIDIA is a key buyer (tier 3; the company has not named NVIDIA as a buyer of this product).
products.how_it_works: Moving the optics next to the chip removes the separate digital signal processor (DSP) in each pluggable module, which cuts power and cost. The laser stays outside, so it can be replaced and kept cool.
products.sales: Not disclosed. Proxy: Components segment revenue $2.01bn in FY2026 (+79.7%). Stifel (2026-10-05, tier 3) reports management saying NVIDIA's ultra-high-power laser requirements 'accelerated into year-end and calendar year 2027' and December demand exceeds shipment capacity.
products.stage: Shipping, early ramp. An eight-wavelength DWDM ELSFP module was demonstrated at ECOC 2026, with availability expected in the first half of 2027 (company release, 2026-09-21).
products.competition: Coherent and other indium phosphide laser makers; the CPO timetable itself is debated (some reports of delay worries, not verified this run).
products.why_investors_care: If CPO takes off, every switch needs these lasers. The shareholder letter calls it 'a major architectural shift'.
products.watch_next: OCP Summit talk on external laser source architectures (2026-10-14); any figure on the call on 2026-11-05.

products.name: 1.6T optical transceiver modules
products.what_it_is: Plug-in modules that convert electrical data into light and back, moving 1.6 terabits per second, twice the 800G generation.
products.analogy: A faster translator at each end of a phone line between two servers.
products.buyers: Cloud companies and AI cluster builders.
products.how_it_works: Eight lanes of 200 gigabits each, driven by Lumentum's own 200G-per-lane lasers.
products.sales: Not disclosed. The company says it 'started production of our next-generation 1.6T modules' (shareholder letter, 2026-10-06). Proxy: Systems segment revenue $1.01bn in FY2026.
products.competition: Chinese makers InnoLight and Eoptolink (the targets of the US Senate bill), Coherent, and others.
products.why_investors_care: Faster modules sell for more, and the shareholder letter claims 'an early market advantage' in signal integrity.
products.watch_next: Any 1.6T revenue or customer comment on the 2026-11-05 call.
